insight: Einarsson v. Canada (ICSID UNCT/20/6) is the first publicly documented ISDS case to rest a claim centrally on proprietary data protected as copyright/trade secret (offshore marine seismic data) as the covered investment, extending Ring 1 toward information-based assets; it is a structural analogue, not a pharma/clinical-data case (seismic/oil-and-gas context is a fingerprint negative signal).
sources: Upreti, Data, Copyright, and Investor-State Arbitration: Insights from Einarsson v. Canada, SSRN 2023 — https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=4328312

insight: USMCA eliminated ISDS between Canada and the United States and the three-year legacy period expired 30 June 2023, so no successor to Eli Lilly v. Canada can be filed under the principal North-American framework; a recurring pharma three-ring case would now most likely arise under older BITs or the CPTPP against non-North-American states. Pre-existing legacy claims (e.g. Einarsson) remain pending.
sources: Kluwer Arbitration Blog, ISDS Under the USMCA: The First Three Years at a Glance, Nov. 2023 — https://arbitrationblog.kluwerarbitration.com/2023/11/25/isds-under-the-usmca-the-first-three-years-at-a-glance/

insight: No publicly known ISDS case has yet asserted pharmaceutical trade secrets or clinical-trial data as the primary covered investment; the Ferguson/Kim framework remains theoretical, confirmed against the UNCTAD ISDS Navigator (through July 2024), italaw, and practitioner commentary. The central open question stays prospective.
sources: Kim, 15 J. Marshall Rev. Intell. Prop. L. 999 (2016)
